evals.prompt: We noticed agents keep adding new troubleshooting notes instead of updating the existing convention. Turn that feedback into a durable instruction update.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the root decision pattern, verifies the merge target exists, merges guidance into the existing source of truth, avoids a one-off retrospective, and validates the update with the four gates.

evals.prompt: An agent once forgot to quote a Windows path containing brackets. Add a permanent rule for that exact path so it never happens again.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the exact-path rule as overfit and instead proposes or writes a general shell path handling principle if an appropriate source of truth exists.

evals.prompt: After a review, we learned that API signatures were assumed instead of verified. Improve the relevant skill or doc so future agents verify interfaces before coding.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing API/interface guidance, rewrites or merges into it, removes redundant wording if needed, and reports the generalized principle plus validation scores.

evals.prompt: Do not edit files. Review this feedback: agents keep naming a merge target from memory instead of checking whether the file and section exist.
evals.expected_output: Uses proposal mode, does not claim a file was updated, verifies any proposed target before naming it, and includes precise proposed text or explicitly refuses to name an unverified target.

evals.prompt: Use the recent conversation context, not a new explicit incident: a forward test exposed that a subagent named D:\skills\AGENTS.md as a merge target without verifying the file, and the user then asked whether the skill can extract feedback loops from context. Improve or propose the durable instruction update.
evals.expected_output: Extracts the feedback signal from conversation context, identifies the root decision failure as unverified context-derived ownership, adds or proposes a general Context Intake rule with exact proposed text, and validates the update without preserving incident-specific wording.
